title: How to Park on a Hill (Part 2)

script.visual_search: car parked on a steep hill slope

script.narration: First, pull close to the curb and stop completely with your foot on the brake. Second, turn your steering wheel sharply toward the curb if you are facing downhill, or away from the curb if you are facing uphill. Third, gently let the car roll until the front tire rests lightly against the curb before setting your parking brake.
script.visual_search: close up of car wheel touching curb

script.narration: Like if this helped, follow for daily driving tips. Have you ever parked on a hill? Comment below, to make sure you never forget to properly align your tires.
script.visual_search: driver setting parking brake in vehicle

description:
Part 2 of Dry Steering Explained! Learn how to properly align your tires when parking on a hill to keep your car secure and protect your steering components.

Essential knowledge for all new drivers in the usa.
why_it_will_work: Continues a high-performing channel series and answers a high-volume search intent for parking tips.
quality_problems: fact-check: Instructing the driver to gently let the car roll until the tire rests against the curb can cause tire and wheel damage, and is not standard safe driving practice.
